predecessors.name: Byzantine Empire
predecessors.text: Gallura began as a Byzantine province; the north-east of Sardinia, main city Olbia, 'subdivided into ten curatoriae governed by curatores under the judge'

successors.name: Republic of Pisa
successors.text: Gallura as enlarged in 1258 (the 1206 outline plus the Ogliastra-Sarrabus third of Cagliari), held by Pisa until the Aragonese conquest of 1323-1324

ledger.x: 866: Gallura appears in Cliopatria's first shape as the north-east of Sardinia; the page dates no founding.
1015: a Dénia army lands in the north of Sardinia.
1016: the Dénia camp is gone after 'one year'.
1206: William I of Cagliari invades Gallura after the death of Barisone II left only a daughter, Elena (1203).
1207: Elena marries the Pisan Lamberto Visconti, who repulses the Cagliari invasion.
1207: the Visconti of Pisa become the judges of Gallura.

1258: Gallura receives the north-east third of the Judicate of Cagliari when Pisa and the other judicates divide it. it.wikipedia (Giudicato di Cagliari): Gallura received 'la parte di nord-orientale (Ogliastra, Sarrabus)'; the English Cagliari page: the territory was 'partitioned in three parts', 'assigned to the…
1287: Nino Visconti is deposed and Gallura passes to Pisa.

wars.name: Dénia invasion of Sardinia
wars.outcome: The Dénia army held a camp in the north of Sardinia for one year; the fleets of Pisa and Genoa reconquered the island; Mujahid's heir Ali Iqbal al-Dawla was captured and ransomed only in 1032.

wars.name: Cagliari's invasion of Gallura
wars.outcome: William I of Cagliari invaded in 1206 and was repulsed by Lamberto Visconti, who married the heiress Elena in 1207.

wars.name: Genoese and Torres attack on Gallura
wars.outcome: In 1211 Comita III of Torres made a treaty with Genoa to conquer the island, Gallura first; Pisa struck back in 1212 after Gallura was attacked; Pope Honorius III forced a settlement on 1 December 1217.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line is on any page opened: the pages give ten curatoriae and the city of Olbia only, and Cliopatria's outline follows modern provinces.
